verdict.rationale: The docs show `getSandbox()` gets or creates a sandbox by ID in a single SDK call, and each sandbox runs isolated in its own VM/container with a full Linux environment. The 'live in seconds' part has no first-party startup-latency figure; the boot-time numbers in the community thread describe commenters' own Firecracker systems, not Cloudflare's. Missing for 10: documented or measured cold-start/provisioning time, and independent hands-on corroboration of fast spin-up.

support.subject: As a developer, I can spin up an isolated sandbox with one API/SDK call and get a live environment in seconds

citations.quote: getSandbox() - Gets or creates a sandbox instance by ID.
VM-based isolation - Each sandbox runs in its own VM
Each sandbox runs in its own isolated container with a full Linux environment, providing strong security boundaries while maintaining performance.
